about: The importer for an Apple Health export: it finds the export's clinical record files and says where and when Apple Health received each. pod.look() and pod.import() call it; an app does not.
capabilities: Finding the documents of an Apple Health export · appleHealthExport.documents()
Saying where an Apple Health record came from · AppleHealthDocument.facts()
Listing an Apple Health export's records before an import · appleHealthExport.index()

glossary.definition: of a document, said to be the work of a party, by `prov:wasAttributedTo`; a pod reads this to say whose word a record is.
the party that wrote a document's content, such as the hospital whose server gave the record. A document is attributed to its author.
one file that an import takes whole and gives to an adapter: a FHIR resource or Bundle in JSON, or a C-CDA document. The pod keeps its bytes.
what a person downloads of their own records: an Apple Health export, or a C-CDA document from a patient portal.
Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources: HL7's standard for health records as JSON.
the part of the runtime that knows one form of export: it says which files are its documents and what the export states about each. `pod.look()` and `pod.import()` try each importer in turn.
one thing `index()` lists for `pod.look()` to count: something an import would bring, with its source's name, its kind or section, and when it was received, each only where the export states it.
a web-style identifier, of which a URL is one kind; Turtle writes one between angle brackets.
the standard name of a file's format, such as `application/fhir+json`; an import offers a document to the adapters of its media type.
one person's records, and what that person has said about them, kept as files in one folder.
one thing said about a person's health, such as an allergy, a medication or a lab result.
one record in FHIR, named by its type and its id, such as `Observation/ldl-1`.
one hospital server, or one document, whose records an export holds.
a party that passed a document on without writing it, as Apple Health does with a hospital's records. A document is never attributed to its transmitter.
